verdict.note: Driven through the real `spex internal session-cursor` verb (the one the hook calls) against a store whose cursors.json already carries a follows map, so the inbox line is not the only line. The writer emits one field per line, and the hook's exact read — a bash while-read loop with a whole-line match, no jq and no subprocess — recovers the position. The follows entry survives the writer's whole-file rewrite, which is why the hook reads this file but never writes it. This probe also caught and fixed a real defect: the verb echoed its own --to argument, so a correctly-ignored advance printed 'inbox -> 2' while the file held 5; it now reads the position back, and the two answers differ exactly when the offer was refused.
